name: numpy_T
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::numpy_T(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a). Original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract; do not narrow tests to this signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: "aten::numpy_T(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a)" (overload "default") and "aten::numpy_T.a(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a)" (overload "a"). Semantics: a unary, zero-copy metadata view that reverses every dimension of the input (0-D and 1-D keep their shape, 2-D swaps both dimensions, n-D is a full reversal). It returns a new tensor object that is not the input object and that shares the input's storage, so a fill_ through the result reaches the same storage as the input (the pytest asserts shared data_ptr, non-identity with the input, and the write-through case). For conjugated and negative-view inputs the pytest compares the result's lazy conj/neg flags, stride, storage offset, view flag and values against the native reference, and the backward path is likewise exercised through torch.autograd.grad and compared with the native reference. The operator is unary with no scalar operand, so broadcast and scalar/tensor overload forms do not apply. Errors remain owned by the Gems pytest: non-Tensor arguments (nested list, python float, None) and a wrong argument count must raise rather than silently produce a view. This definition models only the representative overload; overload-dependent behavior, keyword usage, returns, error behavior, aliasing and mutation support are defined by the original tests. No unresolved **kwargs are used and no defaults are invented.
